record.paper_title: NTN-based 6G Localization: Vision, Role of LEOs, and Open Problems
record.context_brief: multi-satellite RTT timing and frequency compensation
record.original_question: How can single-satellite round-trip-time positioning in a non-terrestrial network (NTN) be extended to multi-RTT positioning with multiple low-earth-orbit (LEO) satellites when each satellite has a different propagation delay, requiring user equipment to adjust uplink timing and frequency compensation for sounding reference signal reception while maintaining closed-loop timing and frequency compensation with the serving satellite?

evidence.quote: While RTT-based positioning serves as a baseline for single LEO positioning in 5G, multi-RTT for multiple LEOs poses certain challenges. Using two-way TOA necessitates compensating for propagation delays across several LEOs, which differ significantly. These differences may exceed tolerable delay spreads in 5G, making it insufficient to compensate for propagation delay only for the serving satellite, as in TNs.

While 3GPP RAN focuses on single satellite RTT, extending it to multi-RTT encounters fundamental challenges. For instance, accommodating multiple satellites necessitates UE adjustment of timing and frequency compensation for SRS reception. The specification needs to permit the UE to momentarily modify UL timing and frequency for SRS transmission while maintaining closed-loop timing and frequency compensation with the serving satellite.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a non-terrestrial wireless network in which a user equipment (UE) on or near the Earth's surface communicates with a constellation of low-Earth-orbit (LEO) satellites. One satellite, designated the serving satellite, maintains a closed-loop timing- and frequency-compensation procedure with the UE: the UE pre-compensates its uplink (UL) transmissions for the propagation delay τ_s(t) and Doppler shift f_s(t) to the serving satellite so that signals arrive at that satellite aligned with its reference time–frequency grid.

Single-satellite round-trip-time (RTT) positioning estimates the UE position from the two-way time of arrival between the UE and the serving satellite. Multi-RTT positioning generalizes this by also measuring two-way times of arrival to N ≥ 2 additional LEO satellites, where the UE transmits sounding reference signals (SRS) that must be received by each of the satellites with propagation delays τ_i(t) and Doppler shifts f_i(t), i = 1,…,N, that differ from τ_s(t), f_s(t) by amounts which may exceed the tolerable delay spread and frequency offset of the underlying 5G/6G numerology.

Problem. Design a protocol and signaling scheme under which:
(i) for each non-serving satellite i, the UE momentarily adjusts its UL transmit timing by an offset Δτ_i(t) and its UL transmit frequency by an offset Δf_i(t) so that the SRS arrives at satellite i within the cyclic-prefix and subcarrier-spacing tolerances;
(ii) throughout these adjustments, the closed-loop timing- and frequency-compensation loop with the serving satellite remains valid, i.e., the serving link is not lost and subsequent UL transmissions to the serving satellite remain correctly pre-compensated;
(iii) the resulting two-way time-of-arrival measurements to the serving satellite and to the N additional satellites can be combined consistently to estimate the UE position.

Specify the offsets {Δτ_i(t), Δf_i(t)} as functions of the satellite ephemerides and UE state, the scheduling of SRS occasions across satellites, and the procedure for restoring the serving-link compensation, and prove that the resulting joint multi-RTT estimator is well-defined and feasible within standard 5G/6G physical-layer tolerances.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent 3GPP Release 18/19 NTN studies and survey literature on 6G NTN localization indicate that multi-RTT positioning with multiple LEO satellites, including UE-side timing/frequency adjustments for SRS toward non-serving satellites while preserving closed-loop compensation with the serving satellite, is identified as an open standardization and research problem; no complete protocol-level solution appears to be published.

status_evidence.title: 3GPP NTN positioning study (RAN1)
status_evidence.snippet: 3GPP Release 18/19 work items on NTN positioning currently focus on single-satellite RTT; multi-satellite RTT remains under study.
status_evidence.claim: Standards bodies have not finalized multi-RTT procedures for multiple LEO satellites.

status_evidence.title: Surveys on 6G NTN localization
status_evidence.snippet: Extending single-satellite RTT to multi-RTT raises unresolved challenges in UL timing/frequency adjustment for SRS across satellites.
status_evidence.claim: Multi-RTT with closed-loop compensation maintenance is identified as an open problem.
